summary: Modern databases and data platforms are rapidly embedding AI/ML capabilities directly where data lives, eliminating the need to move data to external ML infrastructure. Vector search has become a central feature, with adoption growing 377% year over year and forecasts suggesting up to 90% of enterprises will use vector databases in some capacity by the end of 2026, making vector search table stakes across major databases. The leading platforms now combine native vector search, LLM integration (often via managed foundation models), and SQL-native ML inference and training for RAG, semantic search, and predictive analytics.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Snowflake Cortex AI (LLM functions, Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst, ML functions)
databases.description: Cortex AI provides serverless access to hosted LLMs for tasks like summarization, translation, sentiment analysis, and text completion via SQL/Python functions. Cortex Search delivers hybrid (vector + keyword) retrieval for RAG and semantic search, and Cortex Analyst enables natural-language querying of structured data. Snowflake Postgres further extends AI-ready data by unifying the popular Postgres database with analytics and AI on one governed platform.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake supports a VECTOR data type with native vector similarity functions (e.g., VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY) and managed hybrid retrieval through Cortex Search. No third-party extension required.
databases.llm_integration: Native integration with hosted foundation models (e.g., Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, Snowflake Arctic) accessible directly through Cortex SQL/Python functions, plus Cortex Agents for agentic workflows.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based pricing measured in Snowflake credits; Cortex LLM functions billed per token processed, and vector/search services billed by compute and storage consumption.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML, BigQuery vector search, and Vertex AI integration (Gemini)
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets analysts create and run ML models using standard SQL, including regression, classification, forecasting, and remote model inference. It builds RAG and context-retrieval applications using embeddings with vector, text, or hybrid search, and includes BigQuery Graph for relationship analysis. Vertex AI integration brings Gemini and other foundation models directly into SQL workflows.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery provides built-in VECTOR_SEARCH, vector indexes, and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING functions directly in SQL; no external extension needed.
databases.llm_integration: Deep native integration with Vertex AI and Gemini models via ML.GENERATE_TEXT and remote model endpoints, enabling generative AI and embeddings from within BigQuery SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Pay-as-you-go on-demand (per TB scanned) or capacity-based (slots) pricing; ML and generative AI inference incur additional Vertex AI model usage charges.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector extension for vector storage/search and pgai for in-database AI/LLM workflows
databases.description: pgvector adds vector storage and similarity search to PostgreSQL, enabling embeddings-based semantic search and RAG with support for HNSW and IVFFlat indexes. The pgai extension brings embedding generation and LLM calls into SQL, letting developers keep AI workloads close to relational data. This 'keep everything together' approach consolidates operational, vector, and AI data in one familiar database.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native to a Postgres deployment only via the pgvector extension, which is open-source and installable on standard PostgreSQL. Since pgvector is an extension (not core Postgres), vector capability depends on it being enabled; it is the de facto standard and widely available on managed Postgres offerings.
databases.llm_integration: Via the pgai extension, which calls external LLM/embedding providers (e.g., OpenAI, Ollama, Cohere) from SQL; also integrates easily with application-side LLM frameworks like LangChain and LlamaIndex.
databases.pricing_notes: PostgreSQL and pgvector/pgai are open-source and free; costs come from the underlying compute/storage of the hosting provider and any external LLM API usage.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning (in-database inference via SageMaker, Bedrock, and Comprehend)
databases.description: Aurora ML enables SQL-based calls to external AWS ML services to run predictions directly from database queries. It integrates with Amazon SageMaker for custom models, Amazon Bedrock for foundation-model/generative AI, and Amazon Comprehend for NLP tasks like sentiment analysis. This lets applications add inference to transactional queries without moving data out of Aurora.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not natively built into Aurora ML. Vector search on Aurora PostgreSQL is provided only through the pgvector extension, which is separate from the Aurora ML service; therefore Aurora ML itself does not offer native vector search.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock for foundation models and generative AI, and with SageMaker for custom LLMs, invoked through SQL functions.
databases.pricing_notes: No additional Aurora ML charge for the integration itself; you pay standard Aurora instance/storage costs plus the underlying SageMaker, Bedrock, or Comprehend usage fees.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML (SQL-based model creation and inference via SageMaker)
databases.description: Redshift ML allows data analysts to create, train, and deploy ML models using familiar SQL CREATE MODEL syntax, with SageMaker Autopilot handling model training behind the scenes. Models can run supervised learning (regression, classification) and leverage remote inference, and Redshift ML can call Bedrock foundation models for generative AI. It brings predictive analytics to the data warehouse without exporting data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not a native feature of Redshift ML. Redshift has introduced vector-related capabilities and embedding generation, but Redshift ML as a service focuses on model training/inference rather than offering a built-in vector similarity search engine comparable to dedicated vector databases.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock for LLM/generative AI functions and with SageMaker for custom models, all invoked through SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Standard Redshift compute/storage charges apply, plus SageMaker training costs for building models and Bedrock usage for generative AI calls; inference within Redshift uses Redshift compute.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI (model training, serving, agents) and Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Mosaic AI provides a full platform for building, fine-tuning, serving, and governing ML and generative AI models, including foundation model APIs and agent frameworks. Databricks Vector Search offers a managed, serverless vector index tightly integrated with Unity Catalog governance and Delta tables for RAG applications. Together they support end-to-end AI workloads on the lakehouse.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a built-in managed service that automatically syncs embeddings from Delta tables and provides low-latency similarity search; no third-party extension required.
databases.llm_integration: Native Foundation Model APIs and Model Serving for hosted/open LLMs (e.g., Llama, DBRX, Claude via partners), plus Mosaic AI Agent Framework for building RAG and agentic applications.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based pricing in Databricks Units (DBUs); Vector Search and Model Serving billed by compute/endpoint usage, with separate charges for foundation model token consumption.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search for semantic search and RAG on operational data
databases.description: Atlas Vector Search enables storing and querying high-dimensional embeddings alongside operational documents in MongoDB, supporting semantic search, RAG, and recommendation use cases. It uses approximate nearest-neighbor (HNSW) indexing and supports hybrid search combining vector and full-text relevance. Because vectors live next to application data, it simplifies building AI features without a separate vector store.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Atlas Vector Search is a built-in capability of MongoDB Atlas with a dedicated vector index type and $vectorSearch aggregation stage; no external extension required.
databases.llm_integration: No bundled LLM, but integrates with external providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI) and frameworks like LangChain and LlamaIndex for embeddings and RAG pipelines.
databases.pricing_notes: Available on Atlas managed clusters; vector search runs on dedicated Search Nodes billed by instance size/compute, in addition to standard Atlas cluster and storage costs.
